source.filename: Soft robotic grippers A review on technologies, materials, and applications .pdf

actuation: Fluidic elastomer actuators (FEAs) / Soft pneumatic actuators (SPAs)
Passive structures with external motors (tendon-driven and contact-driven deformation)
Ionic polymer-metal composites (IPMCs) / soft electrochemical actuators
constitutive_assumptions: Hyperelasticity in elastomeric bladders and pneumatic network channels
Viscoelasticity in soft polymers (PDMS, hydrogels) exhibiting both loss and storage moduli for dynamic energy dissipation
Purely elastic response in rigid support structures without loss modulus
Infinite degrees of freedom continuum deformation in soft elastomeric bodies
Inextensible layer / inextensible reinforcement threads inducing bending motion upon pressurization
control_variables: Operating environment (ambient air, underwater, clean, dry, wet)
Geometry, mass, and rigidity of grasped target objects
Supply fluid pressure limits and gas volume
Applied voltage and electric field intensity limits
Thermal boundaries and heating current for phase-change or shape-memory materials
dependent_variables: Maximum grasping force, holding force, and pull force
Actuation strain, elongation, and bending curvature
Actuator response time and bandwidth / actuation frequency
Stiffness tuning range and variable stiffness ratio
Fatigue life and actuation cycle durability

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Fluidic elastomer actuators offer compliant deformation and simple fabrication, but external compressors/pumps restrict portability and fluidic channel impedance restricts response frequencies above 1 Hz.
Granular and particle jamming mechanisms achieve rapid transition from compliant adaptation to rigid holding under vacuum, though conforming to deformable items after jamming remains problematic.
Combining soft fluidic actuation with controllable adhesion or jamming enables decoupled shape and stiffness control, supporting payloads up to 100 to 1000 times the gripper self-weight.

Dielectric elastomer actuators achieve actuation strains exceeding 100 percent with high energy density, but typically require high operating voltages and external rigid support frames to maintain stress output.

Underactuation and virtually infinite degrees of freedom in soft continuum structures complicate modeling and control, prompting the use of reduced-order models and SOFA-based numerical simulation frameworks.

Biodegradable gelatin biogels and elastomer formulations achieve ultimate strains over 300 percent and withstand more than 100,000 cycles, showing promise for sustainable or disposable soft robotic tools.

experimental_setup: Tensile force and pull-off holding force testing across diverse object profiles
Bioimpedance sensor integration and measurement setups on fruit models
In vivo biopsy procedures in porcine bile duct models
Deep-sea robotic deployments (including universal jamming grippers on ROV Hercules at 1200 m depth) and shallow-water trials
Cyclic fatigue and durability actuation rigs exceeding 100,000 to 700,000 cycles
Additive manufacturing (extrusion, multimaterial 3D printing, PolyJet) and double-casting elastomer mold configurations
future_work: Establishing standardized characterization and benchmarking protocols for soft gripper performance
Developing accurate reduced-order models (ROMs) and open simulation frameworks to bypass empirical trial-and-error
Advancing multimaterial 3D printing and 4D printing to integrate sensors, smart materials, and time-dependent reconfiguration
Improving untethered operation through compact power supplies, miniaturized pressure sources, and embedded tactile feedback
Expanding commercialization beyond fixture actuation and simple pick-and-place tasks into complex industrial, medical, and agricultural environments
independent_variables: Applied voltage and electric field magnitude
Actuator cross-sectional geometry, chamber patterning, fiber angles, and initial curvature
Material formulation, composite layering, and cellular/TPMS structural topologies
limitations_inferred: The review does not provide new empirical measurements or independently validated constitutive models of its own

Quantitative performance metrics compiled from disparate literature sources cannot be directly benchmarked against each other due to differing experimental protocols, object shapes, and testing conditions
Discussion regarding long-term chemical resilience and degradation of soft materials in harsh agricultural chemicals or marine salinity remains primarily qualitative
limitations_stated_by_authors: FEAs rely heavily on cumbersome, weighty external compressors and pumps, hindering untethered operation, and suffer from limited response frequencies due to channel fluidic impedance
PSEMs present miniaturization difficulties that restrict deployment on compact mobile platforms
DEAs require high voltages, suffer from compliant electrode reliability issues, and exhibit low stress output when rigid support frames are omitted
IPMCs demonstrate sluggish response speeds and relatively low force/stress generation
SMAs have limited actuation strain data reported in literature, suffer from thermal hysteresis, and are restricted to wire or sheet geometries
Granular jamming cannot readily conform to deformable items once stiffened, and low-melting-point alloys exhibit slow thermal response times
Electro-adhesion is vulnerable to contact peeling failure, while gecko dry adhesion performance drops sharply on dusty, irregular, or porous substrates
Continuous deformation and infinite degrees of freedom lead to complex mechanical modeling and under-actuated control challenges, often necessitating repeated trial-and-error
Lack of standardized testing protocols and design automation tools for 3D-printed soft grippers, alongside commercialization barriers tied to controllability and cost
main_results: Systematic categorization of soft grasping into three foundational pillars: actuation, controlled stiffness, and controlled adhesion, alongside hybrid combinations
Demonstration that hybridizing pneumatic actuators with electroadhesion or particle jamming overcomes trade-offs between compliance and holding capacity
Survey of material systems showing silicone elastomers and polyurethanes as dominant, with viable emerging options in biodegradable biogels and bioplastics

Review of successful field implementations across medicine (neuroprosthetics, MIS, swab sampling), agriculture (damage-free crop harvesting), industry (high-speed food packaging), and underwater exploration (deep-sea sampling to 1200 m)
Highlighting reduced-order modeling (ROMs) and numerical frameworks (SOFA platform) as critical pathways to manage computational complexity in continuum soft robot design
modeling_methods: Numerical modeling via the Simulation Open Framework Architecture (SOFA) platform for soft finger bending behavior
Reduced-order models (ROMs) for lowering computational complexity of continuum soft robots while preserving prediction accuracy
Finite element analysis (FEA) and finite element simulations for hyperelastic deformation and contact mechanics
Mathematical modeling of triply periodic minimal surfaces (TPMS) for interpenetrating phase composite stiffness tuning
performance_metrics: Grasping and holding force ranges (reported from 0.12 N up to 164.64 N across reviewed models)
Payload-to-weight ratios (e.g., handling objects 100 to over 1000 times the gripper self-weight)
Actuation strain levels (>100% in DEAs, >300% in gelatin biogels)
Stiffness tuning ratios (e.g., 5.6-fold variation in origami joints; ~90-fold increase using low-melting-point alloys)
Operational bandwidth and cycle speed (e.g., packaging throughput of 3 items per minute; pneumatic actuation limited above 1 Hz)
Durability and fatigue life (>100,000 cycles for electrohydraulic biogels; 200,000 to 700,000 cycles for sleeved bending actuators)
possible_gap_implications: The absence of standardized performance characterization protocols suggests that reported force and payload metrics across soft robotic literature are not directly comparable, demonstrating the need for standardized benchmarking standards
The heavy reliance on trial-and-error design highlights an unmet need for validated, real-time reduced-order and multiphysics modeling frameworks for soft continuum structures
The inherent trade-off between soft compliance and heavy load-carrying capacity indicates that hybrid variable-stiffness mechanisms represent a critical open avenue for high-payload delicate handling
paper.research_objective: To provide a comprehensive review of soft robotic grippers by examining grasping techniques, materials, fabrication strategies, domain applications in medicine, agriculture, industry, and underwater settings, while identifying key mechanical modeling, control, and commercialization challenges.
paper.research_problem: Rigid grippers lack the adaptability and compliance needed to safely interact with humans and manipulate delicate or irregular objects across unstructured environments; meanwhile, soft grippers face persistent engineering challenges in mechanical modeling, actuation trade-offs, miniaturization, material durability, and commercialization.
stiffness_mechanism: Granular jamming / particle pack jamming under vacuum
Shape memory polymers (SMP) with adjustable stiffness joints
Joule heating / electro-thermal variable stiffness of conductive polymers (conductive PLA, TPU)
paper.title: Soft robotic grippers: A review on technologies, materials, and applications
